analysis.title: Coca-Cola Co. (KO): Impressive volume-led Q3 beat & raise, though structural headwinds likely temper EPS growth next year
key_insights: KO Q3 organic revenue growth was +7% y/y vs GS/consensus estimates of +4.3%/+4.4%, driven by concentrate sales +7% and unit case volume +5% (GS est +2.2%/+3.1%). Price/mix was +1% vs the +2.2% estimate.

Concentrate sales ran about 2pts ahead of unit case volumes because of shipment timing, per KO. After Q2 the company had guided to concentrate lagging unit cases by about 1pt. This drove much of the top-line upside.

Q3 gross margin was 62.7%, up about 170bps y/y, vs GS/consensus estimates of 61.7%. Adjusted operating margin was 32.9%, up about 100bps y/y, vs GS/consensus estimates of 33.6%/32.7%. Top-line leverage and currency tailwinds were partly offset by higher marketing and operating expenses.

Q3 comparable EPS was $0.91 (+11% y/y) vs GS/consensus estimates of $0.89/$0.88. The stock traded down 1% on the day. GS attributes this to the valuation premium to peers and to structural and FX headwinds that management expects to temper EPS growth next year.

KO raised FY26 guidance to organic revenue growth of at least about +5% (prior about +5%) and FX-neutral EPS growth of at least +9% (prior +7-8%). Reported comparable EPS growth is at least +11% (prior +9-10%), implying at least $3.33 (prior $3.27-$3.30) vs GS/consensus estimates of $3.30/$3.31 going into the print.
Guidance implies Q4 revenue declines about 1% and Q4 reported EPS grows at least about 1%, vs YTD revenue/EPS growth of about +8%/+13%. Q4 2026 has six fewer days than Q4 2025.

Latin America organic revenue grew +16% (GS est +7.0%, consensus +6.8%), with concentrate +8% and price/mix +7%. EMEA grew +7% (GS est +2.3%, consensus +4.6%), though KO lost value share in a few Western European markets as a hot summer favoured bottled water, where KO underindexes.

North America organic revenue grew +3%, below GS/consensus estimates of +5.2%/+4.7%. KO cited the timing of the July 4 holiday and temporary challenges in certain finished goods businesses, and said trends improved each month during the quarter.

KO's initial FY27 considerations include a slight FX headwind to top and bottom line. Acquisitions and divestitures are an about 8pt revenue headwind and about 2pt EPS headwind, with the pending sale of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa assumed in Q4.

GS lists further FY27 factors: tougher comps against +4% concentrate growth in Q4 2025, easier price/mix comps as affordability initiatives began in Q4 2025, and elevated logistics and transportation costs.

KO expects a decision in the coming months on its litigation with the IRS. The most recent 10-K estimated potential remaining incremental tax and interest liability for tax years 2010-2025 at about $14B as of Dec 31, 2025.

GS keeps its Neutral rating. KO trades at a 45% premium to the market vs a 3-year average premium of 10%, and at about an 11x forward P/E premium to PEP vs a long-term average premium of about 1x. GS sees more favorable risk-reward elsewhere.

GS raised its FY26 EPS estimate by $0.04 to $3.34 and cut its FY27 EPS estimate by $0.02 to $3.49. The 12-month price target rises $2 to $88 (from $86), based on a 24.0x P/E and 19.5x EV/EBITDA. Against the $92.70 price this implies 5.1% downside.
GS models FY26 organic growth as mostly volume-driven, with concentrate sales/unit case volume +4.0%/+4.2%, vs PEP FY26 volumes of +0.7%.
KO's raised FY26 cash flow guidance is operating cash flow of about $15.2bn (prior about $14.6bn) and free cash flow of about $13.0bn (prior about $12.4bn).

market_movers.rationale: Neutral maintained after a Q3 beat and raise. The 45% premium to the market and the structural and FX headwinds for FY27 limit upside. The price target rises to $88 from $86.

earnings_insights: KO Q3 2026 (reported 10/27): comparable EPS $0.91 reported (+10.7% y/y) vs GS est $0.89 and Visible Alpha consensus $0.88. Net sales were $13,354mn vs GS est $12,954mn and consensus $12,877mn.
Q3 2026 organic revenue growth of +7% reported vs GS est +4.3% and consensus +4.4%. Concentrate sales were +7% and unit case volume +5%, both reported, vs GS est +2.2%/+3.1%.
Q3 2026 gross margin of 62.7% reported vs GS est 61.7% and consensus 61.7%. Operating margin of 32.9% reported vs GS est 33.6% and consensus 32.7%.

FY26 guidance (company, issued 10/27): organic revenue growth at least about +5% (prior about +5%). FX-neutral comparable EPS growth at least +9% (prior +7-8%). Comparable EPS growth at least +11% (prior +9-10%), implying at least $3.33. The tax rate is about 19.7%, excluding the IRS litigation.

FY26 estimates (GS): EPS $3.34 (old $3.30), revenue $50,604mn (old $49,844mn), organic growth +5.7%. FY27 GS estimates: EPS $3.49 (old $3.51), revenue $49,300mn (old $50,742mn), organic growth +4.6%, FX-neutral comparable EPS growth +4.9%.

Q4 2026 FX guidance (company): about 1pt FX tailwind to revenue and about 4pt tailwind to comparable EPS, plus an about 4pt/3pt top/bottom-line headwind from acquisitions and divestitures. GS models Q4 2026E EPS at $0.60.

FY27 initial considerations (company): slight FX headwind to top and bottom line, about 8pt revenue headwind and about 2pt EPS headwind from acquisitions, divestitures and structural items. GS models FY27 revenue declining 2.6% reported.
risk_factors: Upside risks to GS estimates and target: an acceleration in US carbonated soft drink volumes, easing FX headwinds and less pronounced competitive pressure.
Downside risks: on-premise exposure headwinds, stepped-up competitive pressure, a material slowdown in carbonated soft drink volumes, ESG pressure around packaging and sugar or soda taxes.

IRS litigation: potential aggregate remaining incremental tax and interest liability of about $14B for tax years 2010-2025 as of Dec 31, 2025, with a decision expected in the coming months. It is not included in the guided tax rate.
Elevated logistics and transportation costs, tougher Q4 2025 comps (+4% concentrate growth) and lost value share in parts of Western Europe.
Structural and FX headwinds, including the pending Coca-Cola Beverages Africa sale, which GS expects to temper FY27 EPS growth.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots historical KO and PEP NTM P/E since 2001, with KO at 28.3x and PEP at 15.9x currently.
vol_and_positioning: KO trades at an FY27E P/E of 26.3x, a 13% premium to its 1-year average of 23.2x and a 19% premium to its 3-year average of 22.1x. Against the beverage peer group it is at a 42% forward P/E premium, vs 33% on a 1-year average and 25% on a 3-year average.

KO trades at an FY27E EV/EBITDA of 23.3x, a 13% premium to its 1-year average of 20.7x and a 19% premium to its 3-year average of 19.6x. Against the beverage peer group it is at a 66% forward EV/EBITDA premium, vs 56% on a 1-year average and 47% on a 3-year average.
NTM P/E is 28.3x for KO and 15.9x for PEP (Exhibit 1). KO shares are up 12.7% over 3 months, 21.0% over 6 months and 33.0% over 12 months, vs the S&P 500 by +8.8%, +12.9% and +17.6% relative.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 organic growth of +7% was volume-led (concentrate +7%, unit case +5%), FY26 guidance was raised, and share momentum is strong. GS models KO FY26 volume growth of +4.2%, well ahead of PEP at +0.7%.
tension_points.bear_case: KO trades at a 45% premium to the market and about an 11x forward P/E premium to PEP. FY27 faces FX and divestiture headwinds, tougher Q4 comps, and a possible IRS liability of about $14B.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS cites an acceleration in US carbonated soft drink volumes, easing FX headwinds and less pronounced competitive pressure as upside risks to its Neutral stance.

theme_stances.theme: KO volume-led growth vs premium valuation
theme_stances.key_argument: Strong volume-led Q3 results and a guidance raise are offset by a rich valuation premium and FY27 structural and FX headwinds, so risk-reward is neutral.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to see a more favorable risk-reward elsewhere
